# Test: tracked-CSV suite-write regression guard

**Parent:** AH-0MVKYQWSW0067F12 (plan phase; test-first item — created first)

## Summary

Add the automated regression guard that proves a full-suite run never modifies the
tracked config CSVs (`src/data/ship-config.csv`, `src/data/enemy-configs.csv`,
`src/data/difficulty-curves.csv`) in **either** the active worktree **or** the main
checkout. This is the acceptance test for the parent bug: it must fail loudly when a
later change reintroduces a leaked CSV write.

## User story

As a developer/agent running the suite, I want the suite itself to assert that no tracked
CSV changed during the run, so a leaked write fails the run immediately instead of tripping
the implement dirty-tree gate hours later.

## Scope

- A Vitest `globalSetup`/teardown pair (new small module, e.g.
  `src/test/trackedCsvGuard.globalSetup.ts` plus a testable helper) registered in
  `vitest.config.ts` for both `unit` and `integration` projects.
- Snapshot the content hash (sha256) of the three tracked CSVs in the active checkout at
  suite start; resolve the main checkout via `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` (worktrees
  share the main `.git`, so `dirname` of the common dir is the main checkout) and snapshot
  its CSVs too when the path differs and the files exist.
- On teardown, compare; if any file changed, throw with the offending path(s), the
  checkout, and the pre/post git diff hint so the failure is actionable.
- A pure unit test for the comparison/reporting helper (changed / unchanged / missing /
  non-git checkout cases) so the guard logic itself is covered without needing a leak.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Parent AC 1 (AH-0MVKYQWSW0067F12) covered by this item:** **No tracked-file writes from suites** — Running the audit-accepted full suite (`npm --silent test`: `unit` + `integration` projects) from a worktree leaves every tracked `src/data/*.csv` (`ship-config.csv`, `enemy-configs.csv`, `difficulty-curves.csv`) unchanged in **both** the active worktree and the main checkout. Verified by an automated pre/post `git status --porcelain` of both checkouts that runs as part of the change's tests (a regression guard the suite itself asserts).

- `npm --silent test` registers the guard for both projects; a full suite run leaves all
  three tracked CSVs byte-identical in the active checkout and the main checkout.
- The guard is proven effective: a deliberate in-test write to a tracked CSV (or a
  temporary mutation performed inside the guard's own unit test) makes the guard report the
  changed file and fail — the check is not vacuous.
- Guard degrades safely: outside a git repository, or when the main checkout path is
  unresolvable, it logs a skip reason and does not fail the run.
- Guard teardown never writes to the watched files and never itself dirties the tree
  (`git status --porcelain` is unchanged by a suite run apart from intended test output).
- The helper's unit tests pass and are included in the existing `unit` project selection.

## Key Files

- `src/test/trackedCsvGuard.ts` — hash/compare/report helper (pure, unit-testable).
- `src/test/trackedCsvGuard.test.ts` — unit tests for the helper.
- `src/test/trackedCsvGuard.globalSetup.ts` — Vitest global setup returning the teardown.
- `vitest.config.ts` — register `globalSetup` for the `unit` and `integration` projects.
- `src/data/csv-seed.test.ts` — reference for the tracked CSV list; do not duplicate logic.

## Minimal implementation (smallest end-to-end slice)

1. Helper: `snapshotTrackedCsvs(repoRoots: string[]) -> Map<path, hash>`,
   `diffSnapshots(before, after) -> string[]` and a formatter for the failure message.
2. Global setup: resolve the active root from `process.cwd()` and the main checkout from
   `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`; return a teardown closure that diffs and throws.
3. Unit-test the helper's diff/format paths, including a real temp-dir mutation.
4. Register in `vitest.config.ts` for both projects; run the changed-scope suite via
   `/skill:test` to confirm green.

## Notes / risks

- Do **not** shell out to `git status` for the assertion (porcelain output is noisier than
  content hashes and cannot distinguish checkouts); use content hashes and keep git only
  for locating the main checkout.
- The guard is expected to be committed **before** the fixes (TDD); it should pass on a
  clean run and only fail if a leak recurs.
- Overlap: `src/data/csv-seed.test.ts` already validates CSV *content* in the active
  checkout; this item adds the cross-checkout write guard, it does not replace the seed
  tests.

# Feature: CSV plugin root isolation and escape refusal

**Parent:** AH-0MVKYQWSW0067F12

## Summary

Replace the CSV dev-server plugin's implicit `process.cwd()` write root with an explicit,
verified root derived from the Vite-resolved project root, and refuse any request whose
resolved target escapes that root (no file I/O, HTTP error plus a logged reason).

## User story

As a test-suite/CI operator, I want the CSV plugin to be incapable of writing outside the
checkout it is serving, so a suite run can never clobber the main checkout's tracked CSVs
through a symlinked `node_modules` / mis-inferred project root.

## Scope

- `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts`:
  - Resolve the root inside `configureServer` as
    `options.root ?? server.config.root` (Vite resolves `server.config.root` from the
    config file's directory, so it stays in the active checkout instead of following
    `process.cwd()`); keep `options.root` as an explicit override for the existing
    temp-fixture tests.
  - Add a containment guard: for both GET and PUT, `resolve(root, relPath)` must stay inside
    the resolved root (`path.relative` check plus a `..`/absolute-path check, not naive
    `startsWith`); otherwise respond `403` with
    `{ ok: false, error: 'target escapes project root' }` and log the reason, performing no
    filesystem access.
  - Update the `ConfigCsvPluginOptions.root` doc comment and the factory doc comment to
    describe the new root semantics.
- `vite.config.ts`: only touch if the plugin cannot self-derive the root; keep
  `configCsvPlugin()` optionless when `server.config.root` suffices.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Parent AC 2 (AH-0MVKYQWSW0067F12) covered by this item:** **Root isolation in the plugin** — The CSV plugin never resolves write targets to a checkout other than the active project root: the implicit `process.cwd()` default is replaced by an explicit, verified root (derived from the Vite-resolved root, or an explicit option), and any request whose resolved target escapes the active root is refused with no file I/O (HTTP error + logged reason). Existing explicit-root test fixtures keep working unchanged.

- With no `root` option, a plugin configured against a fake `ViteDevServer` whose
  `config.root` is a temp dir writes only inside that temp dir — never to
  `process.cwd()` (asserted by a test that sets `process.cwd()` elsewhere and checks the
  cwd CSV is untouched).
- A request whose `relPath` escapes the root (`../` traversal, URL-encoded traversal,
  absolute path) is refused with HTTP 403, no file created/modified on disk, and a
  logged reason; covered for both GET and PUT.
- Existing explicit-root fixtures in `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.test.ts` and
  `src/core/configStore.integration.test.ts` keep passing unchanged.
- Valid in-root writes keep atomic-write (temp file + rename) behaviour and the existing
  upsert/append semantics; `isDevServer`/`apply: 'serve'` gating is unchanged.
- The plugin's own tests pass in the `unit` project selection.

## Key Files

- `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts` — root resolution, containment guard, doc comments.
- `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.test.ts` — new default-root and escape-refusal tests.
- `vite.config.ts` — only if an explicit root must be passed; otherwise untouched.
- `src/core/configStore.integration.test.ts` — regression check only (explicit root path).
- `src/core/csv.ts` — reference for the codec/validation helpers; not expected to change.

## Minimal implementation (smallest end-to-end slice)

1. Move `root` resolution into `configureServer`; keep `options.root` precedence.
2. Add `isWithinRoot(root, filePath)` helper plus a `403` refusal branch used by both
   handlers before any `existsSync`/`readFileSync`/`atomicWrite`.
3. Add the two tests (default-root isolation, escape refusal for GET and PUT).
4. Update the option/factory doc comments; run the changed-scope suite via `/skill:test`.

## Notes / risks

- Do not weaken the guard for the legit dev workflow: `npm run dev` in the active checkout
  must still persist saves to the committed CSVs (AH-0MTZWZ9TE009CVUA).
- Symlink caveat: compare real paths (`realpath`) where available so a symlinked
  `node_modules` cannot make a legitimate active root look foreign — but a *target* outside
  the root must always be refused.
- Guard reads as well as writes (the parent AC says "any request"); this is deliberate and
  should be noted in the code comment.
data.title: Feature: CSV plugin root isolation and escape refusal

# Feature: Test-mode write guard in configStore

**Parent:** AH-0MVKYQWSW0067F12

## Summary

Add a test-harness guard in `src/core/configStore.ts` so `saveShipConfig`,
`saveEnemyConfig` and `saveDifficultyCurves` can never write a tracked repository file
under vitest: in test mode they update the in-memory registry only and perform no network
I/O.

## User story

As a test author, I want store saves under vitest to be hermetic (registry-only, no disk,
no network), so a test can exercise save behaviour without any chance of PUTing through a
live dev server into a checkout.

## Scope

- `src/core/configStore.ts`:
  - Add `isTestMode()` = `import.meta.env.MODE === 'test'`, next to `isDev()`/`isSsr()`,
    with a doc comment explaining why it exists (belt-and-braces against the relative
    `/api/csv/...` fetch resolving against the happy-dom origin).
  - In each save function, after the `isDev()` gate, short-circuit in test mode: apply the
    same registry mutation the success path applies (including the difficulty-curve
    `generation` normalisation), skip `putCsv`, skip `reReadRegistry`, return `{ ok: true }`.
  - Document the resulting save semantics (registry-only in test mode) on the three
    exported save functions.
- `src/core/configStore.test.ts`: direct unit tests for the guard.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Parent AC 3 (AH-0MVKYQWSW0067F12) covered by this item:** **Test-mode write guard in the store** — Under the vitest/test harness (`import.meta.env.MODE === 'test'` detected in `configStore.ts`), `saveShipConfig`/`saveEnemyConfig`/`saveDifficultyCurves` must never write a tracked repository file: they either update the registry only (documented no-op wrt disk, preserving registry semantics used by tests) or route writes to an isolated temp fixture. A direct unit test covers each save function under test mode asserting no file on disk changes.

- Under `MODE === 'test'` (`vi.stubEnv('MODE', 'test')` with `DEV` true), each of
  `saveShipConfig`, `saveEnemyConfig` and `saveDifficultyCurves` resolves `{ ok: true }`
  while performing **no** `fetch` (asserted with a spy/stub that fails the test if called)
  and leaving every tracked CSV byte-identical (hash check).
- Registry semantics are preserved: after a test-mode ship save, `loadShipConfig()` (and the
  equivalent enemy/difficulty accessors) return the saved values; the difficulty-curve
  `generation` normalisation still applies.
- In non-test dev mode (`MODE` not `test`, `DEV` true) the existing write path is
  unchanged: the save still PUTs through `putCsv` and re-reads the registry (asserted with
  the existing fetch-bridge pattern in a temp root).
- Outside dev mode the existing `WRITE_UNAVAILABLE` behaviour is unchanged.
- All new and existing `src/core/configStore*.test.ts` tests pass in their projects.

## Key Files

- `src/core/configStore.ts` — `isTestMode()`, save-function short-circuit, doc comments.
- `src/core/configStore.test.ts` — test-mode guard unit tests.
- `src/core/configStore.integration.test.ts` — reference for the explicit-root fetch bridge
  pattern; adjust only if the guard changes its expectations.
- `src/core/configDefaults.ts` — reference for default ship/enemy values.

## Minimal implementation (smallest end-to-end slice)

1. Add `isTestMode()` beside `isDev()`/`isSsr()` with the rationale comment.
2. Add the guard branch to `saveShipConfig` (registry update + `{ ok: true }`), then mirror
   it for `saveEnemyConfig` and `saveDifficultyCurves`.
3. Unit-test each save function in test mode: no fetch, no disk change, registry updated.
4. One dev-mode control test proving the real write path still runs; run the changed-scope
   suite via `/skill:test`.

## Notes / risks

- Do not gate on `isDev() === false` (that would flip existing dev-mode assertions); the
  guard is an additional, earlier exit for `MODE === 'test'` only.
- A test-mode caller that expects a *failure* result (`ok: false`) must now stub the store
  function or assert the registry-only contract — check `GymPlayer.test.ts`,
  `GymFodderEnemies.test.ts` and gym save tests for such assumptions.
- Documented divergence: in test mode the registry is authoritative and disk is not, which
  matches how the mocked-store gym tests already behave.

# Task: Hermetic fetch handling for relative CSV calls in happy-dom

**Parent:** AH-0MVKYQWSW0067F12

## Summary

Close the escape route at the harness level: in the `integration` (happy-dom) project, a
relative `/api/csv/...` fetch must never reach a stray real server (whose root may be the
main checkout). Install a default fetch guard in `src/test/setup.ts` that refuses such
requests unless a test explicitly installs its own bridge, and document the pattern.

## User story

As a test author, I want an accidental un-bridged `/api/csv/...` call to fail loudly and
locally instead of silently PUTing into whichever server happens to answer
`http://localhost:3000`.

## Scope

- `src/test/setup.ts` (integration project only): install a default `fetch` wrapper that
  - passes non-`/api/csv/` requests through to the native fetch,
  - for `/api/csv/...` requests without an installed bridge, rejects (or returns a
    synthetic `503` with a clear message) naming the test file and pointing at the bridge
    helper, without performing any network I/O.
  - keeps `vi.stubGlobal('fetch', …)` bridges (used by `configStore.integration.test.ts`)
    working: the wrapper only applies when no per-test stub replaced the global.
- Add/centralise a small bridge helper (e.g. `src/test/csvFetchBridge.ts`) so a test opts in
  with one call, mirroring the existing `installFetchBridge` in
  `src/core/configStore.integration.test.ts`.
- Add the documenting comment in the integration tests that exercise real saves: relative
  fetches resolve against the happy-dom origin, so every real save **must** install the
  bridge; note the `configStore` test-mode guard as the second line of defence.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Parent AC 4 (AH-0MVKYQWSW0067F12) covered by this item:** **Escape route closed** — No test can PUT through a live dev-server endpoint by accident: relative `/api/csv/...` fetches in the happy-dom project must resolve against a test-controlled origin (explicit bridge/stub), never a stray `localhost` server that could answer from the main checkout. Add a comment in the integration tests documenting the relative-fetch/bridge pattern and verifying the bridge is installed for every real save.

- In the `integration` project, an un-bridged relative `/api/csv/...` fetch fails the test
  with a message naming the file and the bridge helper; no real network request is made
  (asserted with a native-fetch spy that must not be called).
- `src/core/configStore.integration.test.ts` keeps passing with its explicit bridge and
  temp root; the bridge helper is reused rather than duplicated if that is a pure
  refactor.
- The guard is a no-op for non-CSV requests (e.g. telemetry upload, asset fetches) so no
  existing integration test regresses.
- A comment in the integration tests documents the relative-fetch/happy-dom origin hazard
  and the requirement to install the bridge for every real save.
- Full `integration` project suite passes via `/skill:test`.

## Key Files

- `src/test/setup.ts` — default fetch guard for `/api/csv/...`.
- `src/test/csvFetchBridge.ts` — shared bridge helper (new, small).
- `src/test/csvFetchBridge.test.ts` — unit tests for the guard/helper.
- `src/core/configStore.integration.test.ts` — reuse the helper, add the documenting comment.
- `vitest.config.ts` — reference only (`setupFiles: ['src/test/setup.ts']`).

## Minimal implementation (smallest end-to-end slice)

1. Write the guard helper + unit tests (un-bridged rejection, bridged pass-through,
   non-CSV pass-through).
2. Wire it into `src/test/setup.ts` for the integration project.
3. Reuse it in `configStore.integration.test.ts` and add the documenting comment.
4. Run the changed-scope suite via `/skill:test` to confirm no integration regressions.

## Notes / risks

- `vi.stubGlobal`/`vi.unstubAllGlobals` ordering matters: if the default guard is installed
  at module scope it must be re-installed after `vi.unstubAllGlobals()` in `afterEach`;
  document the resolution in the helper.
- Do not simply hard-stub `fetch` globally — that would break legit non-CSV fetches in

# Fail fast on unwritable --out and invalid tune CSV

## Goal (user story)
As a developer running tune-loop verification I want `--tune` to validate `--out` (and the
balance CSV path) before anything expensive starts, so an invalid path fails in seconds with
an actionable message instead of running both sweeps first and then hanging or dying.

## Problem
`scripts/evaluate.mjs` only touches the output directory after both batches have run:
`executeTune()` calls `mkdirSync(options.outputDir, {recursive: true})` *after* the candidate
sweep (line ~394) and `main()` does the same for the non-tune path (line ~441). The 2026-10-21
negative probe (`--out /proc/nope/x`, 2 games x 200 ticks) therefore ran both sweeps and then
stalled for 166.6 minutes before an external SIGKILL (parent item AH-0MVIKLOOJ0058Z9B).

## Expected behaviour
- `node scripts/evaluate.mjs --tune --set enemy-configs.csv boss.health=7 --games 2 --ticks 200 --out <unwritable>`
  exits non-zero in well under two seconds, printing a single clear diagnostic on stderr.
- The probe runs **before** `loadCore()` (no Vite SSR boot) and before any `--tune` sweep.
- The `--tune` CSV target (`src/data/<tuneFile>`) is validated up-front too: a missing or
  unreadable CSV fails fast with its own message instead of failing after a baseline sweep.

## Implementation sketch (smallest end-to-end slice)
1. Add an exported, unit-testable probe to `scripts/evaluate.mjs`, e.g.
   `ensureWritableOutputDir(dir)` → `{ok: true}` | `{ok: false, code, message}`:
   `mkdirSync(dir, {recursive: true})`, then write + `fsync` + unlink a sentinel file
   (`.evaluate-write-probe-<pid>`) so an unwritable-but-existing directory (`EACCES`) is
   caught, not just a non-creatable one (`ENOTDIR`, `EROFS`).
2. Export a matching `assertTuneInputs(csvPath)` (`readFileSync` probe) for the `--tune` CSV.
3. In `main()`, call the probes immediately after `parseEvaluateArgs`/`--help` handling and
   **before** `loadCore()`; on failure write `output directory not writable: <dir> (<code>)`
   (and the CSV equivalent) to stderr and return a non-zero exit code (2 — same class as the
   existing usage-error exit, documented in `EVALUATE_USAGE`).
4. Keep the late `mkdirSync` calls as a cheap idempotent safety net; do not duplicate the
   validity logic.
5. Update `EVALUATE_USAGE` and `docs/BALANCING.md` (§Tuning loop → "Guards and guarantees")
   with the fail-fast validation, and extend the doc guard
   (`src/ai/eval/balancingDocs.test.ts`) to assert the new statements.

## Key Files
- scripts/evaluate.mjs
- scripts/evaluate-failfast.test.ts
- scripts/evaluate-args.test.ts
- docs/BALANCING.md
- src/ai/eval/balancingDocs.test.ts

## Acceptance Criteria
1. The repro command fails fast (< 2 s) with a clear "output directory not writable" diagnostic and a non-zero exit, demonstrated after the fix (timings quoted in a work-item comment).
2. The writeability probe and CSV-path validation run before loadCore() and before any baseline or candidate sweep, proven by a test that observes no SSR boot on the failure path.
3. An unwritable-but-existing directory (EACCES) and a non-directory path (ENOTDIR) both fail fast, and the --tune CSV path is validated before the baseline sweep.
4. --tune with a valid --out still runs baseline -> edit -> re-run -> compare -> restore and exits 0; existing behaviour is preserved and existing evaluate/tune tests stay green.
5. CLI help (EVALUATE_USAGE) and docs/BALANCING.md mention the new validation, and the docs-guard test asserts it.
6. Unit tests cover the writeability probe and the CLI exit codes for each failure path, run under the project test policy (test skill).

# Journal the tune CSV edit so a hard kill cannot leave it dirty

## Goal (user story)
As a developer I want the tune/edit cycle crash-safe, so that even an external SIGKILL, OOM or
timeout kill of the CLI never leaves `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` edited in the worktree — or,
if it does, the very next invocation (or a documented one-line command) restores it exactly.

## Problem
`executeTune()` applies the edit through `applyCsvEditFile()` and restores it in a `finally`
via `restoreCsvFile()` using the in-memory `attempt.originalText`. A SIGKILL runs no `finally`,
so the edited CSV survives the process (observed on 2026-10-21 immediately after the exit-137
kill, parent item AH-0MVIKLOOJ0058Z9B).

## Expected behaviour
- Before the first edited byte is written, a small journal (target path + original bytes) is
  persisted beside the CSV and fsynced.
- The journal is git-ignored, so a crashed run never shows up as a worktree change.
- After a successful restore (or with `--keep-edit`) the journal is removed.
- Any subsequent `scripts/evaluate.mjs --tune` invocation that finds a stale journal first
  reconciles it (restores the original bytes, removes the journal, prints a warning) and then
  proceeds — so no manual step is needed in the normal case.
- A documented manual repair path exists for the case where the CSV must be restored without
  running the CLI again.

## Implementation sketch (smallest end-to-end slice)
1. New module `scripts/csvEditJournal.mjs`:
   `writeJournal(csvPath, originalBytes)` — write `<csvPath>.tune-journal` (JSON: csvPath,
   base64 original, pid, ISO timestamp) to a temp name, `fsync`, `rename` (atomic);
   `readJournal(path)`; `clearJournal(path)`; `reconcileJournal(path)` — restore original
   bytes when the journal exists, then delete it, returning `{action: 'restored'|'none'}`.
2. Wire into `executeTune()`: write the journal before `applyCsvEditFile`'s write, and clear
   it inside the existing `finally` after `restoreCsvFile()` resolves.
3. `main()` reconciles a stale journal for the `--tune` target before validation proceeds.
4. Add the journal pattern to `.gitignore` (e.g. `src/data/*.tune-journal`).
5. Document the guarantee + repair commands in `docs/BALANCING.md` (§Tuning loop →
   "Guards and guarantees"), and assert it in `src/ai/eval/balancingDocs.test.ts`.

## Key Files
- scripts/evaluate.mjs
- scripts/csvEditJournal.mjs
- scripts/evaluate-failfast.test.ts
- scripts/csvEdit-shell.test.ts
- src/utils/csvEdit.ts
- docs/BALANCING.md
- scripts/evaluate-args.test.ts

## Acceptance Criteria
1. A simulated hard kill (SIGKILL) after the edit leaves a journal; the next invocation restores the CSV byte-identical to the pre-run state, verified by a test that kills a child process and compares bytes.
2. The journal is written (fsynced, atomically renamed) beside the CSV before the edited bytes are written, and is removed after a successful restore or when --keep-edit is used.
3. The journal path is git-ignored so a crashed run leaves no worktree change, asserted by a .gitignore guard test.
4. A deterministic, documented repair path restores the CSV exactly, documented in docs/BALANCING.md together with the journal file name.
5. Unit tests cover the journal write, restore-from-journal and stale-journal reconciliation, run under the project test policy (test skill).
6. Existing tune behaviour is preserved: --tune with a valid --out still runs baseline -> edit -> re-run -> compare -> restore, exits 0, and existing evaluate/tune tests stay green.

# Per-run progress output and opt-in sweep watchdog

## Goal (user story)
As a developer (or an agent) running a long tune sweep I want visible per-run progress and an
opt-in bounded-runtime guard, so an abnormal run can never stall silently for hours and so a
timeout aborts cleanly with the CSV already restored.

## Problem
`--tune` prints nothing between start and the final summary: `executeTune()` runs two
`runBalanceBatch()` sweeps with no output. When the 2026-10-21 negative probe stalled, the only
signal was a silent process for 166.6 minutes until an external SIGKILL (parent item
AH-0MVIKLOOJ0058Z9B). After slice 2 the known hang is gone, but a future stall in the sweep
itself (configuration-driven blow-up, non-determinism guard loop, I/O stall) would again be
invisible.

## Expected behaviour
- Every `--tune` run writes one progress line per completed game to **stderr**:
  `[tune] baseline 1/2 seed=1 policy=competent`, then `[tune] candidate 2/2 …`, then the phase
  transitions (edit applied, comparing, restoring). Stdout stays byte-identical to today so
  artifact/print parity and determinism are preserved.
- `--watchdog <seconds>` (default `0` = off) arms a bounded-runtime guard: on expiry the run
  prints a diagnostic naming the phase and the elapsed time, restores the CSV (journal from
  slice 3 + synchronous restore), and exits with a distinct code (124) rather than leaving a
  killed-but-dirty worktree.
- `--help` and `docs/BALANCING.md` document both.

## Implementation sketch (smallest end-to-end slice)
1. Reuse the existing per-run hook instead of adding a second mechanism: `runBatch` already
   accepts `config.onRun` (`src/ai/eval/engine.ts`), but `runBalanceBatch()` in
   `src/ai/eval/cli.ts` does not expose it (and `CliOptions.telemetrySink` is ignored there).
   Add an optional second parameter `runBalanceBatch(options, hooks?: {onRun?})` that forwards
   `onRun`; keep the existing signature/behaviour when `hooks` is omitted.
2. In `executeTune()`, pass an `onRun` that writes the progress line to `io.err` (count games
   against `sweep.seeds.length * policies.length`) — no divergent copy of the sweep logic.
3. Add `--watchdog <seconds>` parsing to `parseEvaluateArgs` (validated: finite, >= 0;
   non-numeric → usage error exit 2), arm a timer in `executeTune()` and clear it in the
   existing `finally`; on expiry: diagnostic + `restoreCsvFile` + `process.exitCode = 124`
   (use `exitCode`, not `exit()`, so pending stderr drains and the pipe cannot mask the exit).
4. Docs: `docs/BALANCING.md` tune flags table + "Guards and guarantees"; assert in
   `src/ai/eval/balancingDocs.test.ts`.

## Risky assumptions
- A watchdog timer inside a synchronous sweep cannot interrupt a *blocking* synchronous call —
  it only fires between runs. Recorded as an accepted limitation: the guard catches stalls that
  yield to the event loop (the observed case is caught by slice 2's fail-fast path instead), and
  the progress lines remain the primary signal for a truly blocking stall. Document this
  limitation in `docs/BALANCING.md`.

## Key Files
- scripts/evaluate.mjs
- src/ai/eval/cli.ts
- src/ai/eval/engine.ts
- src/ai/eval/cli.test.ts
- scripts/evaluate-args.test.ts
- docs/BALANCING.md

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Every --tune run emits per-run progress lines on stderr (never stdout), covered by a unit test that captures both streams.
2. An opt-in bounded-runtime watchdog (--watchdog <seconds>) aborts the sweep with a clear diagnostic naming the stalled phase, restores the CSV, and exits with a distinct non-zero code, covered by a test.
3. The full verification command used in AH-0MVBNLM2V008XC8T (including the negative probe) completes without hanging, with elapsed times recorded in a work-item comment.
4. Progress wiring reuses the shared runBatch onRun hook through runBalanceBatch (no divergent sweep copy in the shell), covered by cli.test.ts.
5. Artifact/print parity is preserved: stdout and the four tune artifacts are byte-identical to the pre-change output for the same seed/options (determinism tests stay green).
6. --help and docs/BALANCING.md document --watchdog, its default (off), its exit code, and the accepted limitation that a blocking synchronous stall cannot be interrupted, asserted by the docs guard.

# Document and verify the fixed/curve/dynamic mode mix

## Summary / user story

**As a designer**, I want the per-wave generation mode ledger to be explicit and test-pinned, so it is clear which waves are hand-authored for identity/showcase and which are generated for per-run variety (producer Q3=c').

The parent adopts a **mixed** mechanism: authored `fixed` waves where a showcase/pin requires them, `curve` where determinism is wanted, and `dynamic` filler where seeded variety is safe. Today that mix is implicit in the CSV. This feature makes it a documented, verified contract, and converts a filler wave to `dynamic` **only** where the authored data cannot express the intent.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A documented per-wave mode ledger (a table covering all 100 waves: level, wave, mode, and the one-line reason it holds that mode) is published in the GDD's default-campaign note.
2. A test asserts the shipped CSV/config **matches** the ledger: all three modes are used, every recorded showcase/opening/mini-boss wave is `fixed` (or its curated opening mode), and no unlisted wave silently changes mode.
3. For every `dynamic` wave the seeded-determinism contract holds (same seed ⇒ identical campaign; different seeds may differ) and AC1/R1–R3 still hold across a multi-seed sweep.
4. If a filler wave is converted to `dynamic`, the ledger records the conversion plus its reason and the wave remains within the sequencer acceptance band; if no conversion is warranted, the ledger records that decision explicitly as a documented no-op.
5. `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` header comments and `src/core/configStore.ts` comments describe the final mix and link the ledger.
6. Any mode change keeps `shootEnabled` correct for the level (Levels 1–3 off, 4–10 on).


**Parent-AC traceability.** This item discharges the following acceptance criteria of the parent epic (AH-0MVI5XXOU00954EA), restated here so the link is explicit and auditable:
- **Parent AC4** — Generated (`curve`/`dynamic`) waves continue to satisfy the classification balance rules R1–R3 (opening formation-only, no all-chaser wave, bounded ranged mix), verified by the existing `waveBalance` audit/validator tests passing over the rebuilt campaign.

- Generate the ledger from the audit tooling (do not hand-maintain a second copy of the mode data).
- Add a test that cross-checks the ledger against `defaultDifficultyCurves()` and the built campaign.
- Convert at most the filler waves where the authored approach cannot avoid a collision; prefer authored data.
- Update the CSV header and `configStore` comments.

- Authored variety rework — Levels 2–4 (onboarding) and Levels 6–10 (the mix decision can only be finalised once collisions are known).

## Summary / user story

**As a maintainer**, I want one verification item that proves the rebuilt 100-wave campaign is varied, deterministic, balanced and regression-free, so the epic can be reviewed against its acceptance criteria with evidence rather than assertion.

**Parent:** AH-0MVIB7PD50029ZY1 — Background scenes (covers parent AC3: unmistakable warp transition timed to `LEVEL_TRANSITION_SECONDS`; related to AH-0MVNTR89P0022JIU "unmistakable" bar).

## Goal

As a player I want an unmistakable hyperspace "warp" when the background changes between levels, and as a developer I want that effect to be a deterministic, time-boxed, individually switchable module with a testable timeline, so level changes read as a jump through space without ever hurting readability or blocking play.

## Background

Producer answer Q2 (2026-10-25): **Option A — hyperspace-style one-shot** (converging streak overlay + radial scale distortion + brief flash/crossfade), timed to `LEVEL_TRANSITION_SECONDS` (1.5 s, currently exported from `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`). Existing VFX modules show the house pattern to copy: exported tuning constants plus per-layer `*_ENABLE_*` toggles and caller-owned effect registries that are destroyed on `SHUTDOWN` (`src/vfx/endOfRunJuice.ts`, `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts`, `src/vfx/phaseShiftJuice.ts`).

Import direction matters: `PlayScene` imports VFX modules, so a VFX module must **not** import `PlayScene`. The duration therefore moves to `src/core/constants.ts` and is re-exported from `PlayScene` for existing importers.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `LEVEL_TRANSITION_SECONDS` moves to `src/core/constants.ts` and `PlayScene` re-exports it unchanged, so `src/vfx/backgroundWarp.ts` can derive `BACKGROUND_WARP_DURATION_SECONDS` from the same single source (no duplicated literal); all existing importers (`PlayScene.test.ts`, `SceneNavigation.test.ts`) keep compiling without edits.
2. `src/vfx/backgroundWarp.ts` exposes the full timeline as exported constants (streak phase, distortion/scale phase, flash/crossfade phase) whose phases are ordered, non-overlapping and sum to the total duration; a test asserts the sum and ordering so the effect can never outlive the transition window.
3. The effect renders three layers — converging streak overlay, radial scale distortion, brief flash/crossfade into the incoming background — each with its own `BACKGROUND_WARP_ENABLE_*` toggle (following the `ENDOFRUN_ENABLE_*` pattern) and exported magnitudes (streak count, speed, colours, scale range, flash alpha).
4. Deterministic: no `Math.random()` (or a seeded generator) — two runs from the same inputs produce byte-identical layer parameters, asserted by test. Time-boxed and observable: an `update(dt)`-style tick API (no reliance on wall-clock tweens) so a test can advance exactly `BACKGROUND_WARP_DURATION_SECONDS` and assert completion; `isComplete()` is true at the end and never before.
5. Bounded and disposable: a fixed maximum streak count (constant), all display objects inside one container, `destroy()` idempotent, and a test asserts the container/children are gone after completion and after an early `destroy()` (no leaks if the scene restarts mid-warp).
6. `src/vfx/backgroundWarp.test.ts` covers the ACs above; changed-scope tests and `tsc --noEmit` pass.

7. **Parent-AC traceability:** this slice's primary implementation is parent AC #3 — "A "warp" transition effect plays while backgrounds change — timed to the existing `LEVEL_TRANSITION_SECONDS` (1.5 s) transition pause — after which the new level's background is fully shown; the effect is deterministic, time-boxed, and does not block input or wave progression." — specifically the warp effect module itself (deterministic, time-boxed, switchable); the non-blocking wiring is AH-0MVSEBW8L009O3JD; the remaining ACs of this slice are the verification and the collateral work it needs.

## Minimal Implementation

- Write the test file first against the constant/API surface you intend to ship (red → green).
- Implement the effect as Phaser `Graphics` inside a `Container` at a depth just above the background layer and below gameplay (exported depth constant); no new assets and no new dependencies.
- Choose deterministic pseudo-randomness from a small in-module LCG seeded by `(fromLevel, toLevel)` so each level pair looks slightly different but reproducible — never `Math.random()`.
- Drive animation from an explicit `update(dt)`/`tick` call (the scene's `update` feeds it) rather than `this.tweens`, matching the deterministic-boot test harness in `src/test/gameHarness.ts`.
- Keep it visually consistent with `wormholeSpawn`/`phaseShiftJuice` (violet→cyan converging lines, white flash peak).
- Do not trigger it from a scene here — the wiring slice owns the trigger; this slice ships the module plus tests.

**Key Files:**

- `src/vfx/backgroundWarp.ts` — new warp transition module.
- `src/vfx/backgroundWarp.test.ts` — new tests.
- `src/core/constants.ts` — `LEVEL_TRANSITION_SECONDS` + warp depth/colour constants.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — re-export `LEVEL_TRANSITION_SECONDS` (no logic change).

- `src/vfx/phaseShiftJuice.ts` — visual-language reference (read-only).

## Goal

As a player I want the new level's background to arrive with the warp exactly when the level changes (and never mid-level), so each of the ten levels is unmistakably a different place in space while gameplay, input and wave timing are untouched.

## Background

Level changes flow `WaveManager.onEnemyDestroyed()` → `'levelCleared'` → `PlayScene._handleWaveEvent` → `_announceLevel()` + `_startTransition()` (`LEVEL_TRANSITION_SECONDS = 1.5`). Two facts shape this slice:

1. **Two handlers.** The `levelCleared` case is duplicated in `PlayScene._handleWaveEvent` and in `PlayScene._advanceAfterTimeout()` (the wave-timer expiry path). Both must reach the background swap, so the `levelCleared` work is extracted into one helper (e.g. `_onLevelCleared()`) that both call — otherwise a level cleared by timeout skips the swap.
2. **Level is already advanced.** `WaveManager` increments `_levelIndex` *before* returning `'levelCleared'`, so `waveManager.level` during the transition is the **incoming** level: the swap target is `backgroundForLevel(waveManager.level)`, and the warp must finish no later than `transitionTimer` reaches 0 (`_onTransitionComplete()` then spawns the new wave).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. On `'levelCleared'` only — not on `'waveCleared'`, not on `'bossTriggered'`, not per wave — `PlayScene` starts the warp and swaps to `backgroundForLevel(waveManager.level)`; the same code path is reached by both the kill path (`_handleWaveEvent`) and the wave-timeout path (`_advanceAfterTimeout`), with no duplicated background logic between them.
2. The warp is created at `_startTransition()` time for a level change, advanced from the scene's own tick (not wall-clock tweens), and is complete by the time the transition ends: after ticking `LEVEL_TRANSITION_SECONDS` the background's `textureKey()` equals `backgroundForLevel(newLevel)`, `isComplete()` is true, and `_onTransitionComplete()` has spawned the wave on the unchanged frame schedule.
3. Non-blocking: during the warp the player still moves, auto-fires and can teleport, and the transition/wave timer schedule is unchanged — asserted by a test that ticks half the transition while driving input and checks bullets/position, plus an assertion that `transitionRemaining()` is unaffected by the warp's presence.
4. Boss entry keeps the final level's background (documented decision: no swap and no warp on `'bossTriggered'`); asserted by test so the boss arena's backdrop is deterministic.
5. Restart/shutdown safety: starting a new run or shutting the scene down mid-warp leaves no warp container, no stale background and no leaked timer — a subsequent level change behaves normally (tested).
6. New integration suite `src/scenes/PlayScene.background.test.ts` covers ACs 1–5 and the existing `PlayScene` suites (`PlayScene.test.ts`, `PlaySceneHUD.test.ts`, `SceneNavigation.test.ts`, `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) still pass unchanged; full-suite gate is left to the dev-push gate (no ad-hoc full runs).

7. **Parent-AC traceability:** this slice's primary implementation is parent AC #6 — "Tests cover: deterministic level→background mapping, swap fires on level change (not wave), warp effect activates during the transition and completes within its duration, and the background layer does not intercept input; document updates (README, code comments, credits/attribution file with licences, GDD §3.2/§7.1 references as needed); the full project test suite passes with the new changes." — specifically the integration-tests half (swap-on-level-change-only, timing, input non-blocking, full suite); the documentation half is AH-0MVSEC4RS003KQGV; the remaining ACs of this slice are the verification and the collateral work it needs.

## Minimal Implementation

- Write `src/scenes/PlayScene.background.test.ts` first (boot via `src/test/gameHarness.ts`, drain a level to force `'levelCleared'`, use the fixture textures from the shared-layer slice).
- Extract `_onLevelCleared()` on `PlayScene`; both `_handleWaveEvent` and `_advanceAfterTimeout` call it (per the parent's "shared behaviour lives once" rule).
- In `_startTransition()`, take an optional `levelChanged` flag (or compare target level against the currently shown one) to start the warp; keep `_startTransition` otherwise identical so wave transitions are unaffected.
- Tick the warp from `update()` next to `transitionTimer`, and destroy it in `_onTransitionComplete()`/`teardownRunState()` (whichever owns cleanup) so completion and early shutdown are both safe.
- Keep the transition banner, wave timer and telemetry calls exactly as they are (no behaviour change beyond the backdrop/warp).

## Deliverables

  wedges, the outcome and a single result callback. Pause exactly like the
  hold-full choice; pass the frozen fire schedule for the reduced-volume ghost

# Wrap-aware steering and clearance

Parent: "Bot should be aware of screen wrap around" (AH-0MVMISF0Q00314LG) — AC1.

## Goal (user story)

As a **player watching the attract demo**, I want the bot to cross a screen edge
to reach a target that is closer the other way, instead of treating the four
seam edges as walls it must not approach, so its movement looks like a human's
and it stops camping near walls it wrongly fears.

## Context

Both steering evaluators reject a bearing purely because it reaches an edge
inside `wallMargin`:

- legacy `evaluateVector` — `src/ai/botDecision.ts` ("reaches a wall within
  `wallMargin`", `wallMargin: 40` default);
- competent `evaluateDirection` — `src/ai/framework/competent/steering.ts`
  ("Walls: reject a bearing that reaches an edge inside the wall margin",
  `wallMargin: 30` default).

Both also derive the objective bearing from the raw straight line, so a
seam-crossing route to an objective is never even considered. The playfield
genuinely wraps: the player ship wraps at all four edges
(`src/utils/movementModel.ts`), bullets wrap (`src/scenes/core/bulletLifecycle.ts`),
and wrap-aware enemies now fly over the edges too (AH-0MV9G3DZ9003P7P8).

This slice consumes the primitives from the wrap-geometry child
(AH-0MVMISF0Q00314LG's wrap-geometry primitive child) — no seam maths is written
here.

## Scope

1. Remove the wall test from both evaluators: an edge is no longer a hazard, so
   `evaluateVector`/`evaluateDirection` never mark a bearing unsafe merely for
   reaching an edge. Keep clearance meaningful: the distance-to-edge term stays
   only as a *clearance* contribution if it is still useful, and if it is dropped
   the clearance cap semantics are preserved.
2. Steering objectives use the **shortest wrapped path**: the objective bearing
   fed to the fan is computed with the wrapped delta (raw vs. seam-crossing
   duplicate of the objective, whichever is shorter), with the near-tie
   hysteresis from the geometry child so the chosen duplicate does not flip
   every tick.
3. Edge-crossing motion is used deliberately when net-positive (Q2 in the
   parent Appendix) — it falls out of shortest-path selection; no scripted wrap
   manœuvre and no change to the human-like governor
   (`src/ai/botHumanLike.ts`).
4. Update the existing integration assertion in
   `src/ai/botSteering.integration.test.ts` that presumes the bot "never wraps
   the screen" (the brake-to-stop case) so it still asserts a controlled stop
   without asserting the bot cannot cross a seam; add seam scenarios instead.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The four arena edges stop being walls in the steering safety/clearance test:
   neither the legacy `evaluateVector` (`src/ai/botDecision.ts`) nor the
   competent `evaluateDirection` (`src/ai/framework/competent/steering.ts`)
   rejects a direction solely because it reaches an edge within `wallMargin`; a
   unit test per evaluator drives a bearing straight at each of the four edges
   from mid-playfield and asserts `safe === true`.
2. Steering toward an objective uses the shortest wrapped path: when the
   seam-crossing route to the objective is shorter than the raw line, the chosen
   bearing points at the wrapped duplicate; when the raw line is already
   shortest, the chosen bearing is unchanged from today's behaviour.
3. Unit tests cover **each of the four edges** (left/right/top/bottom): the
   wrapped bearing is chosen when it is shorter, and an edge-crossing direction
   is safe when it does not otherwise threaten.
4. Hysteresis at nearly-equal raw/wrapped paths: a test drives a sequence of
   ticks where the two route lengths swap by a tiny margin each tick and asserts
   the committed objective duplicate does not oscillate.
5. The human-like governor's reaction cadence, W/A/D control mapping and human
   thrust presses are unchanged; existing steering/bot integration tests stay
   green apart from the deliberately updated "never wraps" assertion, which is
   re-stated as "still brakes to a controlled stop".
6. The changed-scope test gate passes via `/skill:test` (build → test → commit
   order) with tests written first.

## Key Files

- `src/ai/framework/competent/steering.ts` — `evaluateDirection`, `bearingTo`,
  `chooseSteeringDirection`.
- `src/ai/botDecision.ts` — `evaluateVector` and the legacy target-bearing path.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/steering.test.ts`,
  `src/ai/botDecision.test.ts` — per-edge wrap tests (written first).
- `src/ai/botSteering.integration.test.ts` — updated "never wraps" assertion plus
  seam-crossing scenarios.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/competentBot.integration.test.ts` — wrap scenario.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the wrap-geometry primitives child (shared wrapped delta/bearing +
hysteresis must exist first).

## Out of scope

`wallMargin` removal from tunables, style fitting and the tuning UI (separate
child); aim/intercept, nearest-selection, threat prediction and eval parity
(separate children).

# Seam-aware aim and intercept

Parent: "Bot should be aware of screen wrap around" (AH-0MVMISF0Q00314LG) — AC2
(aim half).

## Goal (user story)

As a **player**, I want the demo bot to aim and fire at an enemy along the
shortest wrapped path — including off one edge to arrive from the opposite edge
— so engagements play out across the whole wrap-around arena.

## Context

Aim maths is raw Euclidean today:

- `bearingTo` (`src/ai/framework/competent/steering.ts`) — `normalise(to - from)`;
- `interceptPoint` (same module) — lead solve on raw deltas;
- the legacy aim/aim-delta path in `src/ai/botDecision.ts` — `atan2` on raw
  deltas.

The enemy side already aims on the torus via `aimVectorToTarget` /
`wrappedAxisDelta` (`src/scenes/core/enemyTargeting.ts`, used by
`Scout.tryFireAimedBullet`), so the bot currently fights a wrap-aware opponent
with a wrap-blind gun — a systematic disadvantage once enemy wrap lands.

## Scope

1. `bearingTo` and `interceptPoint` compute their deltas along the shortest
   wrapped path (per-axis wrapped delta), with the bot's
   `playfieldWidth`/`playfieldHeight`; both accept the wrap model without
   changing their existing signatures' call sites more than necessary (a
   `WrapWorld`/tunables argument).
2. The intercept solve predicts the target on the torus: the predicted point is
   the target's position advanced by its velocity, then the *route* to it is the
   shortest wrapped one, so a lead solution that must cross a seam is still
   produced. Stationary targets reduce exactly to the wrapped bearing.
3. Legacy aim in `src/ai/botDecision.ts` uses the same shared wrapped maths
   (delegating to the shared module, no second implementation).
4. Behaviour is bit-identical when the raw line is already the shortest path.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Seam-aware aim and targeting — aim and target selection run on the torus: `bearingTo`/`interceptPoint` and the legacy aim compute deltas along the shortest wrapped path.
2. Aim runs on the torus: `bearingTo` and `interceptPoint`
   (`src/ai/framework/competent/steering.ts`) and the legacy aim compute in
   `src/ai/botDecision.ts` compute deltas along the shortest wrapped path, using
   the shared wrap-geometry primitives (no copied seam maths).
3. When the wrapped route to a target is shorter than the raw line, the returned
   aim angle equals the wrapped-path angle (test asserts the exact expected
   heading for a target across each of the four edges); firing off one edge
   arrives from the opposite edge.
4. When the raw line is already shortest, the aim angle is unchanged from the
   pre-change behaviour (regression test on a representative non-seam geometry).
5. `interceptPoint` leads a moving target across the seam: a test with a target
   whose velocity carries it over an edge returns the wrapped intercept point and
   converges (iteration count honoured), while a stationary target reduces to the
   wrapped bearing.
6. The legacy decision layer's aim output is byte-for-byte the pre-change value
   for a non-seam geometry (golden assertion in `src/ai/botDecision.test.ts`).
7. The changed-scope test gate passes via `/skill:test` (build → test → commit
   order) with tests written first.

# Wrapped nearest-selection and behaviour distances

Parent: "Bot should be aware of screen wrap around" (AH-0MVMISF0Q00314LG) — AC2
(targeting half).

## Goal (user story)

As a **player**, I want the demo bot to pick and pursue the target that is
genuinely nearest on the torus — and to flee across a seam when that is the
safest separation — so its choices match what a human sees on a wrap-around
arena.

## Context

Every nearest/threshold decision in the competent layer is raw Euclidean:

- `nearestTarget` and `bestWeightedTarget` (`src/ai/framework/competent/goals.ts`)
  — `Math.hypot(point - player)`;
- goal-range gates (boss range, proximity falloff) in the same module;
- `nearestEnemyDistance` and `nearestDistance` helper
  (`src/ai/framework/worldModel.ts`);
- collect/engage/evade distances and the evade flee vector
  (`src/ai/framework/competent/behaviours.ts`), including the
  `repositionRadius`/`longTravelDistance` comparisons;
- the legacy decision layer's distance/closest-approach uses in
  `src/ai/botDecision.ts`.

Consequence today: a mineral one pixel past the right edge is scored as ~940 px
away, a pursuing enemy across the seam is ignored, and `evade` computes a flee
vector that runs *into* the seam instead of away along it.

## Scope

1. Wrapped distance for target selection: `nearestTarget`, `bestWeightedTarget`,
   the boss/enemy proximity gates, `nearestEnemyDistance`/`nearestDistance` and
   the collect/engage/evade distance thresholds all measure wrapped distance.
2. The returned *point* is the target itself (unchanged identity — the caller
   still aims at the entity); only the measured distance is wrapped, so nothing
   downstream needs a "duplicate" concept for targeting.
3. Objectives derived from a target use the wrapped delta (the geometry child's
   helper), so `collect`/`engage` steer across the seam when that is shorter.
4. `evade` flees across a seam when the wrapped separation is the safest/nearest
   escape: the weighted flee vector is computed from wrapped deltas, so fleeing
   away from a shot that arrived across a seam works.
5. Behaviour is unchanged where raw and wrapped agree (regression tests).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Wrapped nearest-selection: `nearestTarget`, `bestWeightedTarget`,
   `nearestEnemyDistance` and the collect/engage/evade distance thresholds
   (`src/ai/framework/competent/goals.ts`,
   `src/ai/framework/worldModel.ts`,
   `src/ai/framework/competent/behaviours.ts`) choose nearest by wrapped
   distance, using the shared wrap-geometry primitives.
2. A test where the raw and wrapped ordering **differ** asserts the wrapped-nearest
   candidate wins (two minerals placed so the seam-crossing one is nearer), on
   both axes, while a same-side pair keeps today's choice.
3. When the wrapped route to an enemy, boss or mineral is shorter than the raw
   line, the derived objective bearing points at the seam duplicate (asserted on
   the chosen intent direction); when the raw line is shortest the intent is
   unchanged.
4. `evade` produces a flee direction pointing away from a shot across the seam:
   a test with a threatening shot near the opposite edge asserts the intent
   increases wrapped separation rather than decreasing it.
5. The `.distance` values returned alongside targets are the wrapped distances (a
   direct assertion), so downstream thresholds (`engageRange`, `collectRange`,
   `repositionRadius`, `longTravelDistance`) compare consistently.
6. The changed-scope test gate passes via `/skill:test` (build → test → commit
   order) with tests written first.

## Key Files

- `src/ai/framework/competent/goals.ts` — `nearestTarget`, `bestWeightedTarget`,
  proximity/range gates.
- `src/ai/framework/worldModel.ts` — `nearestEnemyDistance`, `nearestDistance`.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/behaviours.ts` — collect/engage/evade distances,
  evade flee vector, reposition.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/goals.test.ts`,
  `src/ai/framework/worldModel.test.ts`,
  `src/ai/framework/competent/behaviours.test.ts` — wrap cases (written first).

## Dependencies

Blocked by the wrap-geometry primitives child.

# Seam-aware threat and hazard prediction

Parent: "Bot should be aware of screen wrap around" (AH-0MVMISF0Q00314LG) — AC3.

## Goal (user story)

As a **player**, I want the demo bot to dodge a shot that is about to arrive
across the seam, so it survives what any human sees coming — now that wrap-aware
enemies fire across seams (AH-0MV9G3DZ9003P7P8).

## Context

Threat prediction is raw Euclidean:

- `predictIncomingFire` and `classifyShot` (`src/ai/framework/worldModel.ts`) —
  relative position/velocity of the shot vs. the player, closest approach on the
  raw line; the fire-tell estimate is a straight line from the enemy to the
  player's raw position;
- the competent `closestApproach` solve
  (`src/ai/framework/competent/steering.ts`) used by `evaluateDirection` for
  hazards and incoming fire, and by `hazardThreatensPlayer` / the engage kiting
  gate;
- the legacy path-crossing checks in `src/ai/botDecision.ts`
  (`evaluateVector`'s bullet and fire-tell solves);
- `hazardVelocity` (`src/ai/framework/hazardVelocity.ts`) already clamps
  spurious position jumps (`HAZARD_MAX_ESTIMATED_SPEED = 900`) to filter
  wrap-around/respawn teleports.

Consequence: a bullet that will arrive from the opposite edge is predicted on a
line that starts ~900 px away in the wrong direction, so the bot stands still
and dies to it.

## Scope

1. Wrap the *relative* geometry of the prediction: the shot-to-player separation
   is the shortest wrapped delta (per axis), so closest approach and time-to-
   closest are computed on the torus. Where wrapping changes the problem, the
   predicted approach is taken along the wrapped route.
2. Compute the wrapped route for both in-flight bullets and fire-tell estimates
   (`predictIncomingFire`'s `assumedBulletSpeed` line) so a tell that will fire
   across the seam is classified as threatening.
3. Run the competent `closestApproach` (hazards and incoming fire) and the legacy
   path-crossing solves on the wrapped deltas, sharing one implementation.
4. Re-verify `hazardVelocity`'s clamp: with positions modelled on the torus the
   tracker must still clamp only true teleports/respawns and must not swallow a
   legitimate seam re-entry (which is a real ~width-sized jump in raw
   coordinates). Prefer wrapping the *delta* used to estimate velocity over
   raising the clamp; if a change is needed, cover it with tests proving a seam
   crossing yields the hazard's true velocity and a respawn still yields zero/its
   previous estimate.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Seam-aware threat and hazard prediction: `predictIncomingFire` runs on the wrapped torus.
2. `predictIncomingFire` (`src/ai/framework/worldModel.ts`), the competent
   `closestApproach` solves and the legacy path-crossing checks
   (`src/ai/framework/competent/steering.ts`, `src/ai/botDecision.ts`) operate on
   the wrapped torus, using the shared wrap-geometry primitives.
3. A seam-crossing shot is classified as threatening: a test places an enemy
   bullet just outside one edge travelling inward so its wrapped path crosses the
   player, and asserts `threatens === true` and a small `closestDistance` /
   `timeToClosest` — a raw-line-only view would miss it (assert the raw view
   would give a large distance in the same test as a comment/assertion).
4. A shot on the player's own side of the seam is classified exactly as before
   today's behaviour (regression assertion on distance/time/threatens).
5. The `hazardVelocity` tracker's wrap-jump clamp is re-verified and tested: a
   hazard that crosses a seam between decision ticks yields its true (small)
   velocity rather than a clamped/absurd one, and a genuine respawn/teleport is
   still clamped — so the tracker never double-compensates under the torus model.
6. `evaluateDirection` rejects an unsafe bearing when a seam-crossing shot is
   predicted to intersect it, and `hazardThreatensPlayer` reports a seam-crossing
   hazard as threatening.
7. The changed-scope test gate passes via `/skill:test` (build → test → commit
   order) with tests written first.

# Eval arena wrap parity

Parent: "Bot should be aware of screen wrap around" (AH-0MVMISF0Q00314LG) — AC5.

## Goal (user story)

As a **developer**, I want the headless eval arena to mirror the shipped
wrap-around world, so wrap-aware play actually earns eval credit and eval scores
measure the same physics the bot faces in the game.

## Context

The headless arena (`src/ai/eval/arena.ts`) diverges from the game in two ways:

- **Bullets are culled off-field** — `offField(point, width, height)` with
  `BULLET_MARGIN` retires player and enemy bullets once they leave the playfield,
  whereas the game wraps both (`src/scenes/core/bulletLifecycle.ts`, four-edge
  wrap, AH-0MU960UTE001PTV0).
- **Hostile fire aims at the raw player position** — the enemy bullet is launched
  with `dx = player.x - hostile.x` on the raw line, so no hostile shot ever
  crosses a seam, even though wrap-aware enemies now fire along the shortest
  wrapped path.

Consequence: a wrap-aware bot is scored in a world where the seam does not exist
for bullets, so the epic's behaviour earns no credit and eval-driven tuning is
misleading.

## Scope

1. Wrap player and enemy bullets at the four edges each tick (position-only
   modulo on the playfield period, matching
   `src/utils/movementModel.ts`/`bulletLifecycle.ts`), retiring the off-field
   cull for bullets that are alive by lifetime. Bullet lifetime/expiry semantics
   are preserved.
2. Aim hostile fire along the shortest wrapped path using the shared seam maths
   (`aimVectorToTarget`, `wrapAware: true`) so eval hostile fire matches the
   wrap-aware enemy fire in the game — no copy of the aim maths in
   `src/ai/eval/`.
3. Keep everything else about the arena unchanged (drops, minerals, hit radii,
   metrics), so scores stay comparable; document the parity change in
   `docs/EVALUATION.md` (the fuller docs pass lives in the docs child, but this
   note is required here).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The headless eval arena (`src/ai/eval/arena.ts`) is at wrap-parity with the
   game: enemy bullets wrap at the edges instead of being culled off-field, and
   player bullets do too (matching the game's bullet wrap model), while bullet
   lifetime expiry is preserved.
2. Hostile fire aims along the shortest wrapped path (shared
   `aimVectorToTarget`/wrapped-delta maths, no duplicate implementation), so an
   enemy near one edge fires at a player near the opposite edge across the seam.
3. `src/ai/eval/arena.test.ts` covers the wrapped-bullet case (a bullet crossing
   each edge reappears on the opposite side and is not culled) and the seam-aim
   case (a hostile's launched bullet heading equals the wrapped-path heading),
   plus a regression case proving a same-side shot is unchanged.
4. Eval metrics capture wrap-aware play: a test (or the existing metric
   assertions) shows a bullet that crossed the seam is still counted as a

2. `docs/EVALUATION.md` — document eval wrap parity (wrapped bullets, seam-aware
   hostile aim) and what it means for score comparison.

# Arc pay-offs must land on camera (Hull Full, mini-boss death, boss death)

Child of Scripted scenes for video (AH-0MVPJ3NSK008V5VB), covering parent **AC3** — the part that is still unmet after F6 (AH-0MVRMFVQ6007IC4D) and the recording blocker (AH-0MVTEKPM6003R5NW) were closed.

## Why this exists

F6's session recorded the arc twice but found that **the boss took no damage inside its scene window** while an equivalent standalone probe killed the same setup in ~6.6 s; it was still root-causing when a provider outage killed it, and the `implement.py finish` path then committed its tuning (`bossHitsRemaining: 1`, weapon swaps) **without on-camera verification**. The recording path itself is now fixed (AH-0MVTEKPM6003R5NW), so the arc content can be verified and tuned.

Additional evidence gathered 2026-10-29 with a state probe driving the same setups through the shared `startScene` seam:

- **Humble origins (scene 2):** the mineral hold reached only **2 of 5** in the 11 s window, so the hold-full (Hull Full) resolution did **not** occur — the scene's headline pay-off is missing.
- **Mini-boss (scene 5) / main boss (scene 7):** no death was observed inside the sampled windows; the probe's entity readings were not authoritative (the mini-boss/boss are registered as dynamic entities, so `entities[0]` may be an escort), so the death timing still needs an authoritative measurement.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Authoritative pay-off measurement.** A repeatable measurement (a dev-only probe that reads the live scene state for the *actual* mini-boss/boss entity — e.g. `alive` / `getTotalHp()` / `getHealthFraction()` — and the mineral-hold resolution, or an equivalent frame-based check) reports, per pay-off, whether it lands inside its scene's capture window, with the numbers recorded as a comment.
- **AC2 — Hull Full lands in scene 2.** The humble-origins scene resolves a full mineral hold inside its capture window (or the window/seed/loadout is retuned until it does), and the resolution is the `mineral_scoop` (Hull Full) reward from `setup.mineralReward`.
- **AC3 — Mini-boss death lands in scene 5.** The mini-boss dies inside its capture window.
- **AC4 — Boss death lands in scene 7.** The main boss dies inside its capture window.
- **AC5 — Tuning stays inside the config.** Any fix is authored in `examples/scenes.json` (window length, seed, `bossHitsRemaining`, loadout) — with the matching hermetic pins from F1/F4 updated in the same change; assertions are never weakened to make a video pass.
- **AC6 — Re-recorded proof.** One `npm run capture:scenes -- --config examples/scenes.json --json` run produces a finished WebM (fades verified, seven scenes) whose `--json` payload and the AC1 measurements agree, and the total runtime stays near the agreed ~60–75 s baseline (longer only where a beat needs it).
- **AC7 — Producer review of the footage.** Because "visible on camera" is ultimately a judgement call, the recorded clip path and the per-pay-off timings are handed to the producer, who confirms the three pay-offs read correctly in the video.

## Key Files

- `examples/scenes.json` — the arc: windows, seeds, loadouts, `bossHitsRemaining`, `mineralReward`.
- `scripts/capture-scenes.test.ts`, `src/multiSceneCaptureDocs.test.ts` — the hermetic pins that must move with any tuning.
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` — documented pay-off/verification note if the procedure changes.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by **AH-0MVTEKPM6003R5NW** (multi-scene capture must complete) — now closed; the arc can be recorded end-to-end.
- Related: F6 AH-0MVRMFVQ6007IC4D (record/verify slice, closed with its verification gap documented here).
